requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 must not exchange traffic directly with each other on the shared segment
requirements.summary: After firewalld rich-rule drops were applied on node2 (source 192.168.50.12) and node3 (source 192.168.50.11), bidirectional ICMP between node2 and node3 failed 100% (cmd-7ba3f479b8aa4ab7, cmd-f70f2925990540fd), and a raw TCP connect attempt from node2 to node3:22 timed out with no RST (cmd-a0d22e7c687d4957), confirming a protocol-agnostic block. The block was re-verified after all three nodes were rebooted (cmd-6c109d6e07e44c1b, cmd-fd1c92a058c64410), showing the isolation persisted across restarts.

requirements.requirement: Both node2 and node3 must continue to reach node1 on the shared subnet
requirements.summary: After isolation rules were applied, node2->node1 and node3->node1 ICMP both succeeded with 0% loss, and node1->node2/node1->node3 also succeeded (cmd-7ba3f479b8aa4ab7, cmd-f70f2925990540fd, cmd-366d7e0cc3a941c1). Reachability to node1 was re-confirmed after the reboot cycle (cmd-95899d8386e04f52, cmd-6c109d6e07e44c1b, cmd-fd1c92a058c64410).

requirements.requirement: Establish/confirm a functioning shared L2/L3 segment among node1, node2, and node3 as the precondition for applying isolation (baseline healthy connectivity)
requirements.summary: Static IPs were assigned on 192.168.50.0/24 (node1 eth1 .1, node2 enp8s0 .11, node3 enp8s0 .12) and full-mesh ping succeeded in all directions before any isolation rule existed, establishing the baseline the isolation was later validated against.

overall_summary: The executor established static IPs on the shared 192.168.50.0/24 segment, confirmed full-mesh baseline connectivity, then applied host-based firewalld rich-rule drops on node2 and node3 that block all direct traffic between them (verified via ICMP and a raw TCP connect attempt) while leaving node1 reachable from both. The isolation and reachability pattern were re-verified after a full sequential reboot of all three nodes, with boot-identity changes on every node cross-checked against the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots, giving strong evidence of both correctness and persistence.
limitations: TCP-level isolation was tested only from node2->node3 (nc unavailable, /dev/tcp used); node3->node2 was verified only via ICMP, not an independent TCP probe, though this is a minor gap given the identical symmetric firewall rule.

Restart/persistence evidence is a supplemental protocol independent of the stated task contract (which does not itself require reboot survival); it is reported here for completeness and confidence but not scored as a material task requirement.

Isolation was implemented via host-based firewalld rules on node2/node3 rather than a SONiC-side (node1) switch/port-isolation mechanism; this is an equivalent implementation choice since the task did not mandate a specific enforcement point.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full command timeline: IP-address assignment (cmd-57f0aebefe964ee6, cmd-40d86ab01ab04874, cmd-d5aed476016142e1) and firewalld rich-rule additions (cmd-c66c315a3b644792, cmd-232c756471694463) are all directly tied to the required baseline/isolation outcome. The node-restart evidence protocol (cmd-023c8fc545c542f1, cmd-b9797c446b5b462c, cmd-6b750bd8ed1146c4) is an independent, mandated cross-check, not a task requirement, and each reboot was bounded (single reboot per node, node polled back to health). One byproduct is a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file on node2 and node3 from the `nohup ... reboot >/tmp/reboot.log` command, visible in the after-executor snapshot; this is trivial, low-risk residue directly tied to the mandated restart step rather than an unrelated experiment, so it is a minor, not severe, hygiene ding. No failed services, no unrouted/unreverted troubleshooting mutations, and no weakened security controls were found (package-health and failed-services checks are unchanged/clean before and after in the global snapshots).
